title: S3-informed bounded priority admission for invocation-owned browser targets
classification_rationale: The pinned 2026-09-18 Index assessment distinguishes S2 coordination from absent S3 whole-system operational control; the S3 Profile decision-right invariant informed a bounded resource-admission mechanism on top of unmerged owned-target PR #911. This is not an Index-first prediction, a claim of autonomous S3 ownership, or a current grade change. Original issues #375 and #637 evidence independent concurrency and resource-pressure needs.
next_action: Verified dependent experiment on unpublished original PR #911 head: exact remote 7eba11415aac4dcbf703516f170db6d4e22b24ba passed 344 unit tests (1 skipped) and 3 deterministic real UNIX socket / real CLI / fake-CDP canary runs. Prior experimental version reproducibly retained a killed waiter's queue slot; new daemon handler removes it and cleans concurrent acquisition. No real Chrome proof: available headless binary lacks libglib/libnss etc in executor. Material superiority to a host-side queue and full S3 decision ownership are unproven; request no fork-local/external PR publication without exact current-conversation approval and further source-native/user task evidence. Original PR #911 remains unmerged; investigate S4 within the same original if relevant.
